subject: Urgent: WillowBay private cluster — sustained p95 latency & 5xx spike
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <cto@willowbay.com>, Sanjay Rao <sre@willowbay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: WillowBay private cluster — sustained p95 latency & 5xx spike

Hi Ethan / Sanjay —

We are seeing a sustained p95 increase from ~420ms to ~1.8s on your private VPC cluster since ~15:30 UTC and a corresponding uptick in 502/5xx from 0.2% to 3.7% on inference routes for the clinical summarization model. Traffic profile hasn't changed on your side per the initial telemetry (Sanjay, thanks for the quick check).

Quick notes:
- Impact: customer-facing API responses are slower and intermittent 5xx leading to client retries (observed spike in retries from SDK).
- Primary hypothesis: KV-cache eviction storm combined with decoder stalls under sustained long-context requests.
- Immediate risk: SLA breach if not stabilized before next billing window; potential credit discussion.

I've attached the WillowBay ops playbook and a short Redwood mitigation runbook (both attached). Can we coordinate an immediate mitigation window for low-impact maintenance? Proposed short steps:
1) Apply temporary batching cap and lower max_tokens for high-latency routes
2) Enable model fallback to the quantized variant for bursty requests
3) Draining and rolling of 3 nodes (not full cluster) during a 30-minute window to reclaim KV cache states

Please confirm availability for a maintenance window within the next 4 hours or share any constraints. We'll prepare a short rollback plan and post-mortem template.

Attachments: willowbay-ops-playbook.pdf, redwood-mitigation-runbook.pdf

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Customer Success, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Sanjay Rao <sre@willowbay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <cto@willowbay.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:35:22 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: WillowBay private cluster — sustained p95 latency & 5xx spike

Thanks Naomi — we see the same on our side. Additional details from our ops:
- Spike started ~15:22 UTC, correlates with an increase in average sequence length for a small subset of customers (longitudinal clinical notes ingestion).
- Heap growth on node redwood-vpc-3 prior to elevated latencies. We collected a heap dump and attached.
- We can accept a short rolling restart but request that model fallback be enabled first; restarts are expensive for our internal batch jobs.

Attached: willowbay-heapdump.tar.gz (logs + heap snapshot)

Sanjay Rao
SRE Lead, Willow Bay Health
sre@willowbay.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sre@willowbay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 17:02:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: WillowBay private cluster — sustained p95 latency & 5xx spike

Hi all —

Short-term mitigation plan (safe, reversible):
- Toggle on model fallback to quantized-small variant for the affected route (route id: /v1/clinical/summarize). This will reduce per-token latency ~35% and reduce memory pressure.
- Cap dynamic batching to 64 tokens and set per-request timeout to 10s to prevent long-holding requests from monopolizing exec slots.
- Change kernel-level OOM_score_adj on redwood-vpc-3 and add a soft memory limit on the container (no full restart).

If the above does not improve p95 within 20-30 minutes we propose a rolling drain of node redwood-vpc-3 and a targeted restart of its GPU driver process (not a full node reboot). That should reclaim KV cache fragmentation without a full cluster outage.

Action items:
- Naomi: confirm authorization for the fallback and batching cap (we can implement via canary on 10% traffic).
- Sanjay: provide any runtime constraints for driver process restart window.
- Marissa / Karthik: prepare comms and SLA/credit assessment if we need an extended downtime.

Quoting Sanjay below for context:
> We can accept a short rolling restart but request that model fallback be enabled first; restarts are expensive for our internal batch jobs.

Jonas Weber
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <cto@willowbay.com>, Sanjay Rao <sre@willowbay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 18:10:05 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: WillowBay private cluster — sustained p95 latency & 5xx spike

Ethan — looping you in for executive visibility. Quick summary and ask:
- Impact: elevated p95 (~1.8s) and 5xx ~3.7% across clinical summarize route, started ~15:22 UTC.
- Proposed immediate mitigation: enable fallback to quantized-small on 10% canary traffic, apply batching cap, and if no improvement in 30m perform a targeted driver process restart on node redwood-vpc-3 (planned maintenance window: 02:00–02:30 UTC tonight).
- Tradeoffs: minor regression in generation quality on the canary (we expect <2% delta on ROUGE/clinical fidelity), shorter latencies and restored SLA headroom.

We need a go/no-go for the 02:00 UTC maintenance window to proceed with the restart if the canary doesn't stabilize things. If Willow Bay prefers we can expand canary percentage gradually instead of a restart.

If authorized, Redwood will:
- Run the canary (10%) immediately on our side, monitor p95 and 5xx for 30 minutes, and report back.
- If unstable, execute the targeted restart during the stated window and provide a post-maintenance verification report + runbook notes.

Please reply ASAP with authorization or alternative constraints.

Thanks,
Naomi
